instructor: Instructor is very good at emphasizing what he expects from us. No memorization needed. Only drawback is that course is too basic yet too complicated. How so? Let's explain. First parts of the course is trash high school geography part (calculating time and location in different geometric frames), boring as hell. Well hell would be more fun. But then, after MT fun part begins in which you learn more about space objects, universe, etc. Dr. Baştürk is very respectful and helpful. He is very good at communicating with students.

Strongest::: He is one of the best instructors I have found so far in Bilkent. He is very organized in teaching. He always uploads lecture slides before the class. He provided us sample questions before the midterm exam. He is extremely friendly. He understands very well where students usually get confused and he treats the topics accordingly. The homework, exam questions, review questions - all these things seem very easy cause they are organized in an increasingly difficult way. So it's very easy to solve the first one but somewhat difficult to solve the last one. But there is always a connection and the last question is built upon the previous questions. So it's really fun. And even if you don't understand something in the class, you will always understand that during the homework. Definitely would recommend others to take this course from him.
Weakest::: I don't see any weak point of him but one thing that he might consider. He is so lenient in attendance policy that we hardly had students in class during the final few weeks of the course. Though he is a really high-quality instructor, but to attract the students he should implement a somewhat rigid attendance policy so that students get encouraged to join the class or get afraid to miss the class.

He is an angel. He cares about his students and it is easy to see. He tries to make our lives easier and tries not to impose any unnecessary burden on us.
course:
Strongest::: You will learn many completely new things that you cannot learn from any other courses. If you are a physics, math or engineering student, you should take this course. If you are a humanities student, you should also not be afraid to take this course since to obtain a good grade you don't need rigorous mathematical understanding. All the mathematics is simple and he even gives all the formulas in a cheat sheet during the exam.
Weakest::: This course presents you formula that is not in SI unit. You have to remember(I mean be careful) not just the formula but also the unit. SI unit could reduce the problem. A slightly complicated formula is better than having a formula that just works in a specific unit. Also, if it's possible the textbook of Freedman might be changed. It is not rigorous enough for physics students. I found Carroll and Ostile's textbook is a far better textbook for self-study.
It is better fitting for people from outside the physics department. This is not a physics course, per se, it is much more storytelling and verbal reasoning than calculations.

I have taken this course because I have heard positive things about the course and Özgür Hoca from many people. I am not particularly interested in astronomy/astrophysics, but I thought that this is a physics course and might be helpful and fun (PHYS major here). I would not recommend the course to the people who are not REALLY INTERESTED in astronomy, because myself and a similar friend of mine did not enjoy the course a lot. If you are in a position like me, I would say skip this course. The physics in the course is very limited, so do not consider the course as a hardcore physics course (which is fair because it is not classified as a physics elective anyways). Another reason is that lower limit for A is 91, and the final weighs 50%. This means that even if you got full points from the midterm and the homeworks, a grade of 80 from the final demotes you to an A-. The course content, exams, and homeworks are very straightforward, but keep in mind that a simple mistake in the final might lower your grade.
